title: Frontend DataProcessors
hints: A DataProcessor implements DataProcessorInterface::process($cObj, $contentObjectConfiguration, $processorConfiguration, $processedData) and returns the key/value store it was handed, with its own result added under the name the `as` option gives.

Register it as a service tagged data.processor with an identifier in Configuration/Services.yaml. TypoScript then names that identifier rather than a class, the way the core's own processors are referenced; a fully qualified class name still resolves, because the container is asked first and the class is instantiated only when it holds no such service.

Read the processor's own options from $processorConfiguration and through $cObj->stdWrapValue('option', $processorConfiguration, $default), so every option can be set with stdWrap. $contentObjectConfiguration is the whole content object and belongs to its caller.

Honour the `if` option before doing any work: `if (isset($processorConfiguration['if.']) && !$cObj->checkIf($processorConfiguration['if.'])) { return $processedData; }`. A processor that ignores it runs on every element the TypoScript applies to.
Return $processedData unchanged where there is nothing to add. A processor is one of a chain, and the next one is handed what this one returned.

A processor that has grown a second query beside its list, reads request arguments itself, computes page numbers or re-checks a storage pid for a single record is doing what a plugin is for. The extbase hint states that boundary, and the number of records the element renders is what decides it — a decision taken when the table is designed rather than after an import has filled it.

Read what the installation resolved rather than what a file declares: typo3_configuration_lookup answers a TYPO3_CONF_VARS value as it stands at runtime, after every extension has had its say, which is the half a settings file on its own does not show.
